To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ALMA Spectroscopy Survey in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field (ASPECS) has identified sixteen CO emission line sources, six continuum sources, and that the number counts are in line with expectations from the dust models.
the ALMA SPEC survey has identified 22 3\, mm line and continuum sources, all with optical/near-IR counterparts, and has measured the faint end of 3 mm number count.

we detect 22 sources (16 emission lines and 6 continuum sources) at high significance in the HUDF with the ALMA SPEC survey, and that we obtain 3 mm number count that are consistent with extrapolating the 1.3\ mm counts to 3\ mm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying emission lines and 1--3 mm continuum sources in the ALMA SPEC survey in the HUDF, and deriving the number counts of these sources.
the detection of molecular gas in distant star-forming galaxies and the identification of 3 mm continuum galaxies in the HUDF.
the identification of emission line and continuum sources at 3\, mm, and the statistical interpretation of the results.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 3 mm continuum emission is dominated by dust emission from star-forming galaxies at $z \lesssim 2.5$.
the ALMA SPEC survey has detected 16 emission lines, 6 continuum sources, and 2 line+continuum sources, and has provided the most accurate constraints to date on 3 mm number count at faint fluxes.
we find a number of CO emission lines, and 3 mm sources that have optical/near-in infrared counterparts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we find that the CO luminosity functions of the HUDF are consistent with those of the field, and the number counts at 3\, mm are consistent with extrapolations of those from shorter wavelengths.
ALMA is able to detect faint continuum sources at 3\,millimeters, and is also able to detect faint emission lines at 3\mm.
the ALMA SPEC survey is able to detect CO line emission from galaxies in the HUDF, and the number of sources detected is consistent with the number counts expected for dust emission.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the search for faint emission lines and continuum in ALMA spectral scans can be performed efficiently using a simple algorithm that does not require any prior knowledge of the line width, as long as the line width of the emission line is significantly larger than the velocity resolution.
the search for emission lines in the 3 mm band is feasible, and that the number of detections scales well with the amount of data.
the search for faint line emission in ALMA data is best done with a line search algorithm that accounts for the line-width of the emission lines.
